articles.title: VW faz recall de 73 mil carros elétricos por risco de incêndio | G1
articles.standfirst: Defeito está nas baterias de alta voltagem. A empresa reportou que os proprietários dos veículos afetados receberão uma carta de notificação.
articles.summary: Defeito está nas baterias de alta voltagem. Atravessando crise, empresa tem a terceira chamada de produtos às fábricas deste ano.
articles.body:
A Volkswagen (VW) convocou um recall de quase 73 mil veículos elétricos devido a baterias defeituosas, segundo dados publicados nesta terça-feira (20) pela Autoridade Federal de Transporte Motorizado da Alemanha (KBA).

Cerca de 10 mil veículos, em sua maioria da linha ID da Volkswagen, são afetados apenas na Alemanha.

Outros recalls já estão em andamento no Reino Unido e nos Estados Unidos. No mercado americano, mais de 22 mil unidades do modelo ID.4 são afetadas, segundo autoridades dos EUA.

A preparação do recall alemão já havia sido divulgada na semana passada, após verificações internas de qualidade identificarem que determinadas células de baterias de alta tensão em veículos da família ID não atendem aos requisitos de qualidade.

Segundo a empresa, a causa está relacionada a defeitos de produção de fornecedores e afeta um período limitado de fabricação.

"Em casos raros, isso pode levar a um aumento do estresse térmico nessas baterias; em situações extremas, pode ocorrer um incêndio", informou a Volkswagen na semana passada.

Os modelos afetados na Alemanha incluem os ID.3, ID.4, ID.7 e ID.Buzz produzidos em determinados períodos entre 2022 e 2025 , além do Cupra Born, fabricado pela subsidiária espanhola Cupra entre 2022 e 2024.

A empresa reportou que os proprietários dos veículos afetados receberão uma carta de notificação.

Volkswagen ID.4 Pro — Foto: divulgação/Volkswagen

Como medida imediata de segurança, a Volkswagen anunciou que limitará o carregamento dos veículos afetados a, no máximo, 80% da capacidade até que eles sejam inspecionados por uma oficina autorizada.

De acordo com a montadora, os módulos de bateria afetados não precisarão necessariamente ser substituídos, já que uma atualização de software pode ser suficiente.

Este não é o primeiro recall da empresa em 2026 relacionado a baterias. Em março, Volkswagen e Cupra já haviam convocado mais de 90 mil veículos em todo o mundo pelo mesmo motivo, sendo 28 mil deles na Alemanha.

No fim de setembro, a montadora também chamou mais de 5 milhões de veículos para reparos, devido a um parafuso do sistema de direção suscetível à corrosão.

A Volkswagen vem passando por uma crise mais ampla, com ameaças de cortes de empregos e fechamento de fábricas.

As causas mais comumente apontadas incluem o aumento dos custos de produção, o enfraquecimento do mercado interno, a concorrência da China e uma estratégia vacilante para veículos elétricos.

articles.title:
Acipi inicia agendamento de 
cortes gratuitos do 5º Cabelovers | G1
articles.standfirst: A quinta edição do Cabelovers oferece cortes gratuitos em troca da doação de mechas para a confecção de perucas destinadas a pacientes oncológicos
articles.summary: A quinta edição do Cabelovers oferece cortes gratuitos em troca da doação de mechas para a confecção de perucas destinadas a pacientes oncológicos
articles.body:
Os cortes gratuitos ocorrerão na próxima segunda-feira, dia 26, das 9h às 17h, na sede da Acipi — Foto: Crédito: Acipi

Um simples ato que pode trazer conforto em um momento sensível. Essa é a proposta do Conselho da Mulher Empresária da Acipi (Associação Comercial e Industrial de Piracicaba) ao promover a quinta edição do Cabelovers, iniciativa que oferece corte gratuito a quem deseja doar mechas para a confecção de perucas destinadas a pacientes oncológicos. A ação será realizada na próxima segunda-feira (26), das 9h às 17h, na sede da entidade, e está aberta à participação de mulheres, homens e crianças. O agendamento pode ser feito pela bio da Acipi no Instagram: @acipiracicaba

Para participar, é necessário doar mechas de cabelo com, no mínimo, 15 centímetros. Cabelos tingidos e grisalhos também são aceitos. Idealizado pela cabeleireira Valéria Alleoni e realizado em parceria com a Acipi, nesta edição, o CME ampliou o número de profissionais para atender ao maior número de doadores. Serão quatro cadeiras de corte durante todo o dia. Quem participar do Cabelovers terá a oportunidade de conhecer o projeto Almofadas de Coração, realizado pela Loja Tear, que confecciona almofadas em formato anatômico de coração. E, também, colaborar com a doação de tampinhas plásticas para o projeto Mama Amiga. A Mary Kay estará presente durante todo o dia com maquiagem gratuita às participantes.

Para Mauricio Benato, presidente da Acipi, mais do que contribuir para a confecção de perucas, a doação representa a possibilidade de ajudar pacientes a se reconhecerem diante do espelho com mais confiança em um período de tantas transformações.

“Pelo quinto ano, estamos preparando nosso hall para receber os doadores de mechas de cabelo, profissionais da beleza e voluntários em torno de uma causa que une cuidado e empatia”.

As mechas arrecadadas são transformadas em perucas para pacientes em tratamento oncológico — Foto: Crédito: Acipi

No 5º Cabelovers CME Acipi, Valéria Alleoni contará novamente com o apoio da cabeleireira Adriana Balarim.

“Ter a Acipi como parceira nessa iniciativa é fundamental para ampliar o alcance da ação. Nosso desejo é receber muitas doações, porque sabemos o impacto que isso tem na vida de quem está em tratamento. Ver alguém se olhar no espelho com confiança novamente é o que me move. Cada peruca representa uma esperança renovada”, destaca Valéria.

Silvanete Neves, coordenadora do Conselho da Mulher Empresária da Acipi (CME), destaca que o Cabelovers traduz, na prática, o espírito de solidariedade da programação do Outubro Rosa na entidade.

“Quem doa uma mecha talvez enxergue apenas alguns centímetros de cabelo, mas, para quem está enfrentando um tratamento contra o câncer, a doação pode representar autoestima, acolhimento e um pouco mais de confiança para atravessar esse período sensível”, afirma.

Crianças, mulheres e homens podem doar mechas com, no mínimo, 15 centímetros — Foto: Crédito: Acipi

A programação do Outubro Rosa do CME começou no dia 14 de outubro, com o 122º Encontro da Mulher Empresária da Acipi, que teve como tema Escolha-se Hoje! e promoveu uma roda de conversa sobre prevenção, saúde da mulher, envelhecimento saudável, nutrição e bem-estar.

O encontro reuniu o médico Sérgio Bruno, especialista em oncologia ginecológica e mastologia; a geriatra Daniela Nasciutti; e a médica Ana Carolina Figueiredo de Castro, especialista em Ecoendoscopia e Nutrologia. A mediação foi conduzida pela jornalista Daniele Ricci, e a programação contou com trilha sonora da Momento Musical Escola de Música e o Espaço Mulheres que Inspiram, dedicado à apresentação de negócios liderados por empreendedoras.

Nesta quinta edição, o CME ampliou o número de profissionais para atender mais doadores de mechas — Foto: Crédito: Acipi

Local: sede da Acipi (Rua Prudente de Moraes, 459, Centro)

O que: doação de mechas de cabelo a partir de 15 centímetros, inclusive tingidos

Participação: Gratuita e aberta ao público

articles.title: Suspeita de aplicar golpes na venda de passagens aéreas é presa | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre as vítimas estão pessoas do Piauí. Segundo a polícia, bilhetes eram cancelados dias antes do embarque, sem devolução do dinheiro às vítimas.
articles.summary: Entre as vítimas estão pessoas do Piauí. Segundo a polícia, bilhetes comprados com milhas eram cancelados dias antes do embarque, sem devolução do dinheiro às vítimas.
articles.body:
Uma mulher de 34 anos, suspeita de aplicar golpes na venda de passagens aéreas emitidas com milhas , foi presa na última segunda-feira (19), no bairro Cidade dos Funcionários, em Fortaleza . Entre as vítimas estão pessoas do Piauí. A prisão ocorreu em uma ação integrada entre as polícias Civil do Ceará e do Piauí .

Natural do Pará, a suspeita - que não teve a identidade revelada - vendia passagens aéreas de classe executiva que, segundo a polícia cearense, seriam emitidas com milhas. No entanto, os bilhetes eram cancelados dias antes do embarque , sem que os valores pagos pelas vítimas fossem devolvidos. Os pagamentos eram feitos por meio de transferências via Pix.

Também foi cumprido um mandado de busca e apreensão contra a suspeita, que resultou na apreensão de um celular. O aparelho será periciado para auxiliar as investigações.

Ela foi presa por suspeita de estelionato qualificado mediante fraude eletrônica e falsa identidade e foi conduzida à sede da Delegacia de Repressão aos Crimes Cibernéticos (DRCC), onde ficou à disposição do Poder Judiciário.

articles.title: Hellen Patrícia faz show em homenagem a Marília Mendonça | G1
articles.standfirst: Apresentação especial no Sesc Teatro Casa Isaura Campos, em outubro de 2026, celebra o legado da 'Rainha da Sofrência' e os 40 anos de carreira da cantora paraense.
articles.summary: Apresentação especial no Sesc Teatro Casa Isaura Campos, em outubro de 2026, celebra o legado da 'Rainha da Sofrência' e os 40 anos de carreira da cantora paraense.
articles.body:
Hellen Patrícia da Banda Xeiro Verde — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Uma das vozes mais marcantes da música paraense se prepara para homenagear um dos maiores fenômenos do sertanejo nacional. Nesta quarta-feira (21), a cantora Hellen Patrícia, consagrada à frente da banda Xeiro Verde, apresenta o show especial "Hellen Patrícia Canta Marília Mendonça", em Belém .

O espetáculo é no palco do Sesc Teatro Casa Isaura Campos, localizado no bairro do Reduto, a partir das 19h. O tributo promete unir a força interpretativa da artista paraense ao repertório inesquecível da eterna "Rainha da Sofrência".

A apresentação carrega uma forte carga emocional e simbólica. Em novembro de 2026, a morte trágica de Marília Mendonça completa cinco anos.

O show idealizado por Hellen Patrícia é uma celebração à força, à sensibilidade e ao legado musical deixado pela compositora goiana, que revolucionou a música sertaneja e o "feminejo" no Brasil.

Para conduzir essa homenagem, Hellen Patrícia empresta sua experiência de aproximadamente 40 anos de carreira dedicados à música. Conhecida pelo público paraense por liderar multidões ao som do tecnobrega e do ritmo caliente da Xeiro Verde, a cantora agora mergulha no universo do sertanejo romântico.

O repertório do show foi selecionado para emocionar o público, reunindo clássicos que atravessaram gerações e se tornaram trilhas sonoras da vida de milhares de fãs. A promessa é de uma noite memorável, marcada pela nostalgia, respeito e muita emoção na capital paraense.

articles.title: Can a humanitarian crisis in Gaza be averted?
articles.summary: The World Food Programme says it is forced to cut aid for thousands in the enclave.
articles.body:
The United States brokered a “ceasefire” to end Israel’s war on Gaza last year. More than two million people in the enclave were hoping it would change the humanitarian situation there.

But since then, Israel has not stopped its attacks. And the already scarce food supply is about to be strained even further.

The World Food Programme says funding shortages are forcing it to cut back its operations in Gaza.

That means half a million Palestinians there will no longer receive badly needed food aid.

articles.title: Pescador captura peixe de 26 quilos e mais de 1 metro no Acre; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Marcos Venicius, de 33 anos, levou cerca de 20 minutos para tirar um peixe pirarara do Rio Juruá, em Cruzeiro do Sul, no sábado (17).
articles.summary: Marcos Venicius, de 33 anos, levou cerca de 20 minutos para tirar o peixe pirarara da água do Rio Juruá, em Cruzeiro do Sul, no último sábado (17).
articles.body:
“Se acalma, se acalma! Deixa ele cansar”.

O conselho de um amigo resume a tensão de uma pescaria que terminou com muita comemoração. É que o pescador Marcos Venicius, de 33 anos, capturou uma pirarara de pouco mais de 1,20 metro e 26 quilos no Rio Juruá, em Cruzeiro do Sul , no interior do Acre, na tarde do último sábado (17). ( Veja vídeo acima )

Nas imagens, os amigos aparecem acompanhando a disputa até que um deles se aproxima da margem e ajuda. Assim que a pirarara é capturada, Marcos comemora a conquista.

Ao g1 , o pescador contou que usava uma vara simples, de R$ 92, indicada para peixes bem menores e que levou cerca de 20 minutos para tirar o animal da água.

“Jamais imaginei que poderia pegar um peixe deste tamanho. Foi até uma sorte grande porque não estava com o material devidamente apropriado”, contou.

Marcos Venicius, de 33 anos, levou cerca de 20 minutos para tirar o peixe da água — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Marcos pesca desde os 20 anos, mas disse que, naquele dia, a ideia era apenas passar o tempo. Por isso, deixou em casa os equipamentos mais pesados e levou uma vara indicada para peixes de aproximadamente 10 a 12 quilos.

A surpresa veio quando sentiu a força do animal. No primeiro momento, ele chegou a pensar que poderia ser um boto.

“Inicialmente, achei que poderia ser um boto, mas, quando fisguei e senti a força, vi que era um peixe. Mantive a calma e só percebi que era uma pirarara quando ela estava a uns 10 metros de distância'', detalhou.

A partir daí, começou uma disputa de aproximadamente 20 minutos. Enquanto Marcos tentava controlar o peixe, os amigos acompanhavam a movimentação e davam orientações para que ele não se precipitasse.

“Quando fisgou e eu consegui trabalhar o peixe e trazer ele até a beira do rio, dei pulos de emoção! Um sonho realizado”, relembrou.

Boa parte da pirarara foi doada a famílias mais carentes — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A captura também foi resultado de outras tentativas. Segundo Marcos, ele e os três amigos que estavam com ele já vinham passando dias na pescaria, na expectativa de conseguir um peixe daquele porte.

Por isso, apesar de ter sido ele quem capturou o animal, o pescador divide a conquista com os companheiros.

“Realmente é um sonho capturar um peixe de tamanha expressão, um verdadeiro ‘troféu’. A captura foi especial porque eu e meus amigos já vínhamos dias e dias tentando, até conseguirmos êxito. Então, não é um troféu só meu, é um troféu da minha equipe”, afirmou.

Depois da comemoração, o peixe também teve um destino solidário. Segundo Marcos, parte da pirarara foi doada a famílias mais carentes , e apenas uma pequena quantidade ficou com o grupo.

“Geralmente, fazemos a doação para famílias mais carentes. Mas a grande maioria dos peixes a gente solta de volta no rio”, completou.

articles.title: Bristol breakthrough could transform science for blind people
articles.summary: A Bristol-made device displays complex data in braille, helping blind people study and work in STEM.
articles.body:
A blind university lecturer says a new braille device could help people with sight loss study and work in science, technology, engineering and maths (STEM).

The Canute Scientific has been created by Bristol Braille, a not-for-profit company that builds specialist technology with braille users.

Designed to display complex scientific and mathematical information in braille, it is hoped the device will help break down barriers for people pursuing STEM subjects and careers.

For Bath Spa University lecturer Hollie Baker, the technology could make a significant difference. "It is essentially a computer, with a multi-line braille display integrated into it," she said.

Former Conservative MP admits assaulting man

Beach motorbike race made 'as extreme as possible'

'I entered foster care at 14 and it saved my life'

The Canute Scientific looks similar to a computer keyboard, but contains rows of holes through which braille dots move up and down, allowing users to feel information displayed on screen.

"The braille shows exactly the same thing as is on the visual screen. This means you can do things like edit text files – or custom apps to view data," said Baker.

Across the UK, about two million people are living with sight loss , including around 340,000 people who are registered blind or partially sighted.

Baker said accessing information while teaching had previously been difficult.

She had found it "challenging" to refer to her notes while delivering a lecture smoothly.

"Without multi-line braille, I'm relying on either a single line of braille which is like reading through a letterbox, or synthetic speech. And I find having speech babbling in my ear puts me off."

The idea for a system of using raised dots to represent letters and numbers, to be read using your fingers, was first invented by French teenager– Louis Braille – back in the 1820s.

Since then, it has transformed the lives of millions of people around the world, allowing them access to a world which was previously completely inaccessible.

Bristol Braille is the not-for-profit company behind the invention of the Canute Scientific.

The company was founded and managed by Ed Rogers who says these machines are changing lives, for the better.

"Braille is traditionally embossed into paper," he said.

"It's a series of dots making up a single character. Those constitute anything in text, numbers, music scores but there is an issue when it comes to getting that digitised.

"The Canute Scientific has a braille display on the front.

"There are slots through which the dots come, representing the braille characters and that is representing data in the same way that a visual monitor is."

Chris Turner has been working at Bristol Braille for about a year.

He describes himself as blind and says the machines they're making here are transforming lives.

articles.title: Russia, sensing victory, cheers Trump’s latest shift against Ukraine
articles.summary: The Kremlin is counting the Trump administration’s latest turn against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as a major triumph and, coupled with political...
articles.body:
The Kremlin is counting the Trump administration's latest turn against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as a major triumph and, coupled with political upheaval in Europe, a sign that Western support for Ukraine is finally crumbling.

In the 10 days since Vladimir Putin last spoke by telephone with the American president, Donald Trump has announced a sanctions waiver for Russian diesel supplies to the global market, throttled Ukraine's access to vital battlefield satellite systems, put sweeping new sanctions against Russian on hold, as well as moved even more firmly to Russia's side by calling for Zelensky's ouster and holding up supplies of critical interceptor missiles.

On Monday, Trump blasted the Ukrainian president again, saying it was "time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine."

The stakes seem higher than ever. Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff is set to travel to Oslo on Tuesday to meet Zelensky, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store. Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, is expected to participate via video link.

"The aim is to put diplomatic efforts on a more constructive path," Store said.

Zelensky said on Sunday that if Washington aligned with Russia, Ukraine would not survive.

"If the United States will support Putin - it's unbelievable, it's a tragedy," he told NBC News' "Meet the Press" on Sunday. "If these two countries will be together, of course we will not prevail. And we will not be able to stand."

While the European leaders and Zelensky might hope to use the Oslo meeting to steer the Trump administration to a tougher stance against Moscow, Kremlin officials have been crowing that victory over Ukraine is on the horizon, and that Trump's recent moves are steps toward an ever-closer alignment between Washington and Moscow.

Trump's recent ratcheting-up of pressure on Zelensky could mean the U.S. president is again seeking to strong-arm the Ukrainian leader into a deal on terms favorable to Moscow.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Tuesday that Witkoff is expected to brief Putin following the Oslo talks.

Earlier, Peskov said Ukraine's recent resumption of strikes on Russian oil refineries - in defiance of Trump's demands - showed Zelensky's administration in its death throes.

"Some final signs of agony are being observed," Peskov said. "The Kyiv regime is resisting. But this cannot change the course of events."

"Checkmate," Kremlin special envoy Kirill Dmitriev posted triumphantly.

In Moscow, members of the Russian elite said that Putin, a former KGB officer, once again managed to turn the U.S. president.

Putin has decades of experience charming and manipulating foreign leaders, and has demonstrated a consistent ability to flatter Trump and pull him on side, analysts and officials said.

This time, they said, the Russian leader preyed on Trump's fears over low approval ratings and sky-high energy prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, offering a deal on Russian diesel fuel that will supply just a fraction of America's daily consumption and have no impact on prices.

On Friday, the average U.S. diesel price continued to climb to $6.33 per gallon, an increase of about 5 cents per gallon from the previous week.

"Russia's leaders have achieved a certain political victory," said a Russian academic close to senior Russian diplomats, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive diplomacy. "All this happened after their telephone call. Probably Putin was able to convince Trump."

Putin, the academic added, "probably conducted this conversation very professionally and prepared his arguments well."

Mikhail Khodorkovsky, once Russia's richest man and now an opposition leader in exile, said recent events followed a pattern in Putin's relations with Trump.

"I am absolutely convinced that they believe that they managed to take advantage, as they always do; they are opportunists," Khodorkovsky said. "In this case, they believe they have waited for the moment of Trump's additional weakness and [taken] advantage of it."

"For Putin, everything that is happening today are signs of the West's weakness," he said.

Dmitriev, the special envoy, and other Russian officials hailed the diesel deal and Trump's waiving of tough sanctions that were to be imposed under a bill adopted in honor of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, a firm GOP supporter of Ukraine, as steps toward broader Russia-U.S. economic cooperation.

Historically, Russia and the U.S. have never been big economic partners, with Russia exporting little of interest to the U.S. market.

"There is a whole range of economic and investment projects being discussed with the American side that will be implemented," Dmitriev told a Russian energy forum last week. "Our list of projects being discussed with the American side also includes various projects in the Arctic, energy projects, LNG [liquefied natural gas] projects and other areas."

"More and more Americans, including within the administration, understand that sanctions harm the United States itself," he added.

In July - after years of Putin refusing to drop his maximalist demands in Ukraine - Trump finally seemed to side with Zelensky, telling reporters he was doing "an amazing job" and even backing Ukraine's deep strikes on Russian oil refineries.

"It's an escalation, but it's also an escalation that can help lead to an end" of the war, Trump said.

But as the U.S. conflict with Iran dragged on, keeping upward pressure on global oil prices, and as the midterm elections drew ever nearer, the Trump administration suddenly turned again.

After an Aug. 31 meeting with Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov at a Group of 20 event in Asheville, North Carolina, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries as the reason for surging fuel prices - rather than the war in Iran.

It was then easy for Putin to recruit Trump into sharing that viewpoint, some observers said.

"The simplest explanation is that Trump was simply interested in having a talking point for the midterms on diesel, that he has a deal to lower it, said Daniel Fried, a former assistant secretary of state for Europe during George W. Bush's administration.

"I think it is just Trump lashing out because he's feeling cornered and unhappy with the midterms, and Zelensky stood in his way," Fried said, especially after Zelensky publicly derided Trump as "weak" after he announced the diesel deal.

"Trump then extended his frustration to add pressure and try to force a settlement based on a great power deal with Putin, who is skilled at playing his more gullible interlocutors," he said.

That Trump and Putin share a view that strongmen should dominate a world divided into spheres of influence made it even easier for Putin, Fried added. "Trump appears to have been attracted to this view for decades," he said. "And therefore, Ukraine is expendable on strategic grounds, in Trump's view, and it was standing in the way of a perfectly good campaign talking point."

Trump's latest swing toward Putin was hardly surprising, said a former senior U.S. intelligence official.

"It almost doesn't matter what he says, because Trump just seems like he's very eager. He's a very receptive audience," the former intelligence official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive matters.

"If you look at the longer-term trends, he has clearly a preference for Putin over Zelensky, and that transcends any kind of temporary relaxation of the tensions that he has with Zelensky."

"He likes strong authoritarian leaders," the official said. "And deep down, there is this underlying belief on his part that Ukraine cannot win this war, that Russia is bigger, Russia is stronger, Russia is going to crush Ukraine if that's what it takes."

Signs point to Trump seeking to strong-arm Ukraine into a deal by December, when Trump has invited Putin to join him at the G-20 leaders' summit in Miami, said Andrew Weiss, a Russian expert at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Washington.

"The only way I can explain it is that it's connected to the milestones leading up to the meeting of the G-20 in December," Weiss said. "I feel like what's going on here is not really about diesel or refinery long-range strikes. It's really about Trump thinking that he can push the Ukrainians into some sort of political settlement."

The Russians have "tried to use the administration as a battering ram to get the Ukrainians to surrender Donbas," Weiss said, referring to the swath of eastern Ukraine coveted by Putin.

"But then that only opens up a subsequent conversation about constraints on Ukrainian military capabilities," he added, or other underlying Russian demands. "The administration has repeatedly misdiagnosed what the Russians want, and the Russians don't make that easy because they don't say exactly what they want."

articles.title: The Trip's Rob Brydon originally against fictional version of himself
articles.summary: Rob Brydon and Steve Coogan initially thought playing fictionalised versions of themselves was "passé".
articles.body:
Actor and comedian Rob Brydon has said he was initially against the idea of playing a fictionalised version of himself in The Trip, but ended up enjoying it and thought it made viewers "more curious".

The 61-year-old, known for his role as Uncle Bryn in Gavin and Stacey, stars alongside Steve Coogan in the comedy series as exaggerated versions of themselves.

Directed by Michael Winterbottom, it follows the pair as they travel around the world and dine at different restaurants.

Brydon said he and Coogan originally thought the idea was "a bit passé" but eventually concluded that Winterbottom was right to suggest it.

Speaking ahead of the series' season five premiere in London, Brydon said despite his initial hesitation, he enjoyed playing a heightened version of himself.

"When [director Michael Winterbottom] first suggested it, we were both against the idea of playing versions of ourselves," he said.

"But in fact, as ever, Michael was right because it just gives the show... you're more curious about it. Is that how they really are?"

Brydon, who grew up in Baglan, Port Talbot, is often seen engaging in competitive mimicry of famous actors, such as Michael Caine, Al Pacino and Hugh Grant, in the programme.

"When we have a meal, it's not combative," Brydon said.

"We don't do impressions to each other, or if we did, we would never argue over that. It's all just for comic effect.

"But then there are other times when I suppose [our characters] are pretty close to us.

"But you just do little tweaks and you do little extracts, so there'll be grains of truth.

"We just exaggerate it until it becomes funny."

The Trip has covered different locations through the years, with its first season in 2010 set across north England, while other instalments have included Italy, Spain and Greece.

The latest season, titled The Trip to the Northern Lights, is set in Scandinavia, as the duo move from Swedish hotels to remote Norwegian fishing huts while searching for the aurora borealis .

Speaking of the weather conditions while filming, Brydon said "it wasn't that cold, apart from when we went into the Arctic Circle", adding that the scenes were "so breathtaking that you didn't mind the cold".

Brydon previously said he and Coogan found themselves "stripped down" to their underwear "quite a lot" during filming, as the pair immersed themselves not only in dramatic scenery but also in Scandinavian traditions.

"We also stripped down to our pants quite a lot," Brydon told The Times.

"There were plenty of saunas and cold plunges in crystal Nordic waters," he said, describing it as "wonderful".

A release date for The Trip to the Northern Lights is yet to be announced.

articles.title: Sunny Hostin re-visits 'problematic' Kamala Harris answer on 'The View' as hosts question her 2028 potential
articles.summary: Sunny Hostin called Kamala Harris' answer on "The View" a "problematic" moment, revealing exactly what she expected the vice president to say.
articles.body: "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin revisited her widely-discussed 2024 question to former Vice President Kamala Harris during an event on Monday, calling the former Democratic presidential nominee's answer and refusal to distance herself from former President Joe Biden at the time "problematic." Brian Teta, the talk show's executive producer and host of its "Behind the Table" podcast, selected the moment as Hostin's most memorable on the show. He said it was a "seminal moment" in the 2024 election cycle. Hostin described the question as a "gift" and said she thought Harris would have to distance herself from Biden because of his approval ratings at the time. She also said "The View" was the perfect venue to ask the question, calling the liberal show's audience "her people." "I actually thought the answer was going to be, you know, ‘We had a lot of wins in this administration. I was there for those wins, but I, as a woman of color, as a child of immigrants, as I have a different lived experience, and I intend to bring that lived experience with me into the White House. I will do this. I will do that. I will do this. I will do that. I will do that.’ That was what I was expecting. I was not expecting, 'Not a single thing comes to mind.' And I knew honestly when she said it that it was really problematic," Hostin said. KAMALA HARRIS CALLS TO EXPAND SUPREME COURT, ADD STATES IF DEMS TAKE CONGRESS The co-hosts noted that the moment was discussed in books published after the 2024 election, including Harris' memoir, "107 Days," and was also featured in a political ad for President Donald Trump. In "107 Days," Harris wrote that she had no idea she had just "pulled the pin on a hand grenade," with her answer to Hostin's question. She wrote that her staff was beside themselves. "Stationed at various places around the set, my staff were beside themselves. Political operatives have an eye to see a moment, and I could kick myself for giving the other side that moment. During the commercial break, while I was having a bit of fun with some young students I’d noticed in the audience who were obviously playing hooky, offering to write notes to their teachers after the show, Opal [Vadhan] passed me a note from our team, telling me to return to that question and mention that a big difference would be that I would put a Republican in my cabinet," she wrote in her book. 'THE VIEW' CO-HOSTS CAST DOUBT ON KAMALA HARRIS VIABILITY AS 2028 CANDIDATE Teta and the co-hosts said they all knew her response was going to be a problem. Co-host Ana Navarro said Harris' staff "ran" because staff members knew immediately that Harris needed to return to the question and address her answer. KAMALA HARRIS FACES DEMOCRATIC DOUBTS OVER 2028 AS ALLIES PUSH BACK ON CLAIMS SHE’S SQUANDERED HER CHANCE During the show on Friday, both Navarro and Haines said they wouldn't tell Harris not to run, but questioned if she would be the best option for the Democratic Party. "If the Democrats want to win, I don't think she's the right candidate because I think the Democrats have been screaming for new energy. They've been saying we need something new to combat this. This would be her third time on this ballot. From the first time when she didn't ... she was out really early when she ran, and then the time with Biden, this would be the third time. People are clamoring for fresh energy, and there's a lot of candidates," Haines said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Co-host Joy Behar has said on several occasions that she doesn't think the U.S. would elect a woman as president, citing Harris and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton's losses to Trump. She has said the 2028 Democratic presidential nominee should be a man if the party wants to win. Hostin questioned whether president would be the right position for Harris during an April episode of "The View" and said she wished Harris had pursued a run for California governor. "This goes right to the heart of what the Media Research Center has been arguing to the FCC about for months now. The View knowingly operates as a propaganda arm for the Democratic Party and for Democratic candidates," NewsBusters associate editor Nicholas Fondacaro told Fox News Digital in a statement. "Sunny openly admitted that her intention with the question was to help Kamala with what she felt was a layup question that would lead to a slam-dunk answer. This incident was an abuse of ABC's privileged access to the public broadcast spectrum."

articles.title: Two men rearrested on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence service in RAF Fairford incident
articles.summary: British counterterrorism police said Tuesday they have rearrested two men in their investigation into last month’s incident at RAF Fairford in England, where US B-1 bombers were based.
articles.body: British counterterrorism police said Tuesday they have rearrested two men in their investigation into last month’s incident at RAF Fairford in England, where US B-1 bombers were based. A 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old dual British-Iranian national were rearrested on suspicion of assisting Iran’s foreign intelligence service, police said in a statement. “So far seven men have been arrested in connection with our investigation,” Laurence Taylor, a senior counterterrorism police officer, said in a statement. “As a result of the ongoing efforts of our officers, earlier today two of those men were re-arrested for offences relating to Section 3 of the National Security Act — assisting a foreign intelligence service.” “This is very much a live investigation, and our evidence gathering continues, but at this time our position remains the same; we consider it highly likely that there is Iranian state involvement,” Taylor added. The other five men are currently out on bail. Police have not released the names of any of them. In late September, British authorities announced the initial arrest of five men “on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act” and explosives offenses near RAF Fairford, a British air base long used by the US Air Force. Army bomb disposal units and police officers swarmed the area and evacuated civilian homes around the base. Earlier this month, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford was “almost certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard.” Iran has firmly rejected the accusations. US President Donald Trump praised the arrests at the time, telling reporters that the US had worked with Britain and that the men arrested were planning to do “big damage” to RAF Fairford. “We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” Trump said. US intelligence had tracked planning by Iranian groups to target US assets at the base weeks ahead of any arrests, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter. Residents around RAF Fairford also may have tipped authorities off. One resident, who asked to remain anonymous, told CNN that she had called police after seeing three vans surrounded by eight to 10 masked men blocking her driveway. In an interview with Sky News, British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting thanked the woman for making the emergency call. He mentioned that she had only a “partial picture” and offered no further details. Developments at the base did not end there. Days after the initial arrests, the US moved all of its long-range bombers from RAF Fairford following an unspecified threat, a knowledgeable source said. At the time, Trump and Vice President JD Vance hinted that a threat against US assets had prompted the move. “I think we can say that — I mean, they didn’t fly out by accident,” Trump said. “There were some threats, and rather than tempting the enemy, we’ll capture the enemy and beat the enemy. But why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit.” Vance said the move was made “out of an abundance of caution,” suggesting it was a response to a potential threat from Iran even as he declined to detail the specific concerns. As of Tuesday, none of the US bombers had returned to Fairford. This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: In 1933, California built Santiago Creek Dam to create Irvine Lake; 93 years later, the 750-acre reservoir is being lowered ahead of a five-year project that will drain it entirely before rebuilding key dam structures
articles.summary: Orange County’s largest freshwater lake is set to remain empty for five years as local water managers prepare to drain Irvine Lake for major safety
articles.body: Orange County’s largest freshwater lake is set to remain empty for five years as local water managers prepare to drain Irvine Lake for major safety repairs to a 93-year-old dam. The 750-acre reservoir was created in 1933 after the Santiago Creek Dam was built. It will begin a gradual drawdown this month. According to reporting by SFGATE, the Irvine Ranch Water District will lower the lake’s water level from 735 feet to about 720 feet. This will reduce the amount of stored water from 2,800 acre-feet to just 300 acre-feet. The remaining water will stay in the lake until next summer. Contractors will then drain the basin completely to begin structural repairs on the aging dam. he five-year construction plan aims to improve aging infrastructure, address safety risks identified by regulators, and increase the lake’s long-term water storage capacity.Upgrading an extremely high hazard damThe California Division of Safety of Dams has classified the Santiago Creek Dam as having an "Extremely High" downstream hazard level. Because of structural weaknesses, state inspectors have limited the maximum amount of water the lake can hold in recent years. Official details published by project managers on the Santiago Creek Dam website describe several major improvements:Building a new, modern concrete spillway to handle heavy runoff. Reinforcing and strengthening the main earthen dam.Replacing the outlet tower that controls water flowing into and out of the reservoir.According to statements from the Irvine Ranch Water District reported by SFGATE, the improvements will restore the lake to its original design capacity of 28,000 acre-feet. This will allow local authorities to collect and store much more rainwater during major storms.Managing storm risks and drawdown timelinesThe drawdown schedule takes seasonal weather preparations and long-term construction plans into account. Local water managers said lowering the lake is also necessary to prepare for expected winter weather. John Fabris, spokesperson for the Irvine Ranch Water District, explained the plan in an email statement cited by SFGATE. “Drawing down the lake’s levels ahead of El Niño will ensure we have enough space in the reservoir to accommodate major storms and keep the downstream community safe,” Fabris told SFGATE. Fabris added that winter rainfall could temporarily raise the lake’s water level in the coming months. However, crews will repeatedly lower the stored water back to 300 acre-feet before draining the lake completely next summer. “Ultimately, one of the benefits of the Santiago Creek Dam Improvement project is that it will allow us to take advantage of future big storms and capture more rainwater, adding to the community's water supply,” Fabris noted.Local angling impacts and environmental concernsPlans to drain the lake have raised concerns among local freshwater anglers. Irvine Lake is a popular fishing spot along the shore in Orange County, where boating, swimming, and camping are not allowed. Members of the local fishing community have raised questions about what will happen to the lake’s fish, especially non-native white sturgeon, which are protected by catch-and-release rules. Anglers have filed formal appeals with regional water quality control boards, asking for an organised plan to move the fish and prevent them from dying during the draining process. In response to these environmental concerns, Fabris explained that all fish species in Irvine Lake were introduced through stocking programmes rather than arriving through natural migration. “There are no native fish in Irvine Lake,” Fabris told SFGATE. He confirmed that the water district is working with state wildlife officials and fish experts from the California Department of Fish and Wildlife to discuss possible plans to relocate the fish. The water district confirmed that public shoreline fishing is expected to return after construction is complete and the reservoir has been refilled. articles.title: Jane Dodds standing down as Welsh Liberal Democrats leader
articles.summary: Dodds said it was time to hand over the leadership to a "new generation" after nearly nine years in the role.
articles.body:
Jane Dodds has announced she will stand down as leader of the Welsh Liberal Democrats.

Dodds said she would remain the party's only Member of the Senedd (MS), but that work to increase its presence in Wales' parliament "should be led by a new generation".

"Leading the Welsh Liberal Democrats has been the honour of my life," she said in a statement on Tuesday, adding "now is the right time" to hand over the role.

Only Welsh Lib Dem MP David Chadwick is eligible to seek nomination to replace Dodds at this stage, the party said.

Relations between Dodds and the UK Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey were strained after he previously called her leadership into question.

The Liberal Democrats have been represented by just one member in Cardiff Bay since 2016, initially by former Welsh Lib Dem leader Kirsty Williams and later by Dodds since 2021.

Dodds, who represents Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd in the Senedd, is a former social worker who was made her party's Welsh leader in November 2017.

She made headlines last year by getting the previous Welsh Labour government to agree to a greyhound racing ban and £1 bus fares for under-21s in return for helping it pass its budget.

In 2024 Lib Dem leader Sir Ed asked Dodds to reflect on her position over her handling of a sexual abuse case when she worked for the Church in England.

A 2021 report found Dodds made a "grave error of judgement" by not organising a meeting to discuss a particular case of abuse by a late former bishop who sexually abused at least 18 victims over a 15-year period.

Dodds accepted there were "shortcomings", but said she would continue as leader.

After nearly two years of cool relations over the matter, Davey backed Dodds before May's Welsh Parliament election, describing her as an "excellent member of the Senedd" who deserved to be re-elected.

Nominations to replace Dodds will open on 23 October and close on 16 November.

"After May's election, I've thought hard about what our party needs," she said.

"Wales needs more than one liberal voice in the Senedd.

"Building that team will take years of hard work in communities across the country, and I believe that work should be led by a new generation.

"Now is the right time to hand it over."

Brecon, Radnor and Cwm Tawe MP Chadwick said Dodds had "given an enormous amount to the Welsh Liberal Democrats and to public life in Wales, and she deserves our sincere thanks for her service as leader".

"There will understandably be questions about what comes next.

"Today should be about Jane and her contribution to our party.

"I will make a statement about my own political future in the coming days."

Welsh Liberal Democrat president Tim Sly said Dodds had "led our party with warmth, determination and integrity through some of the most turbulent years in Welsh and UK politics".

"She leaves the Welsh Liberal Democrats stronger in our communities and ready to build," he said.

Chadwick requires the support of 50 party members to be the only candidate to replace Dodds and take over as leader.

Should that not happen, or he were to decide not to run, all members on the party's approved parliamentary candidates list could then throw their hats into the ring.

articles.title: As Macron visits Gulf, can France forge its own energy-for-security future?
articles.summary: President Macron’s Gulf visit aims to address rising energy prices and strengthen ties amid regional security concerns.
articles.body:
President Emmanuel Macron has arrived in Bahrain during his tour of the Gulf region, as France continues to reel from a wave of violent protests.

The French leader is hoping to strengthen defence ties and secure oil and gas supplies amid major disruption to global fuel shipments arising from the US-Israel war on Iran. He has already visited Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) as part of his three-day trip. His next stop is Qatar.

On the first day of Macron’s trip, France and Kuwait signed eight agreements and cooperation documents covering defence, artificial intelligence, investment and more.

Macron then met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi on Monday. The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to advancing cooperation in energy, advanced technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

According to the French Foreign Ministry, the UAE is France’s biggest importer in the Gulf, with bilateral trade standing at 10.8 billion euros ($12.1bn) in 2025. According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) [ PDF ], France supplied 18 percent of the UAE’s arms and defence imports in 2025 – the second highest after the United States, at 42 percent.

Andreas Krieg, a senior lecturer at King’s College London’s School of Security Studies, explained that Macron’s visit to the region is “symptomatic of a much larger geopolitical transformation”.

“We are witnessing the gradual emergence of a post-American Middle East in which Washington remains militarily powerful but increasingly struggles to exercise the political leadership it once enjoyed,” Krieg told Al Jazeera.

“Europe and the Gulf now face a remarkably similar strategic challenge. Both have become excessively dependent on American security decisions, and both are discovering that this dependence carries substantial economic and political costs.”

Most pressing for Macron is finding solutions for strife at home.

France has been engulfed in protests and violence over a proposed government budget seeking tens of millions of euros in savings to public spending. Protesters angry about the crumbling state of French schools and planned pay freezes for public-sector workers have taken to the streets in increasingly violent protests, and authorities have imposed curfews in some cities.

More than half a million people gathered across France on Saturday as protesters demanded better education infrastructure and government steps to address the cost-of-living crisis. During weeks of protests, more than 2,500 people have been arrested, and demonstrations have descended into looting and arson in numerous locations.

A major issue is the spike in energy prices affecting all of Europe – much of it as a result of the Iran war – which has also fuelled growing public anger in France. Disruptions to the supply of refined oil products such as petrol and diesel caused by the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz have caused up to 20 percent of French petrol stations to run out of both at various times since the conflict began.

Macron’s visit to the Gulf, accompanied by senior executives from France’s two biggest energy groups, TotalEnergies and Engie, comes as oil prices hover above $100 a barrel.

What France needs most urgently, therefore, is new suppliers. Those look to have been secured.

On Tuesday, the UAE committed to supplying 100,000 tonnes (746,000 barrels) of diesel per month to France for an unspecified duration, according to Bloomberg.

Bahrain has agreed to supply 100,000 tonnes of diesel per month for an unspecified duration, while Saudi Arabia will provide 95,000 tonnes in each of October and November, via TotalEnergies.

Besides securing oil imports, however, France is also looking to boost its own exports, particularly of its defence equipment to the Gulf region, as the country suffers from record national debt – the highest level since the immediate aftermath of World War II, analysts say.

France has already strengthened its military partnership with Saudi Arabia, which has been battling the Iran-backed Houthi group from Yemen.

Last month, Macron said France would send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port of Yanbu, which is crucial for energy transport. Oil installations and airports in Saudi Arabia have come under attack from the Houthi group.

In late September, Macron said France would deploy what he termed “military means” to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Yanbu Red Sea oil terminal. Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which carries oil from its eastern oilfields across the Arabian Peninsula to the Red Sea, has come under attack during the Iran conflict. It is the country’s main means of continuing to export oil while the critical Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted. But Yemen’s Houthis have also been attacking Saudi ships in the Red Sea.

Macron stated in a TV interview that “soldiers, radars, defence systems” would be sent.

While he did not give specifics about volumes, it was a move described by French newspaper Le Monde as marking “a geopolitical shift”, as defence cooperation between the two countries has previously been “discreet, ambiguous and marked by extreme caution when it came to defining it”, the newspaper noted.

Last week, France’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Pascal Confavreux, said again that “operational elements” to defend Saudi oil facilities had been put into action, without specifying which “military means” had been sent.

Meanwhile, on Monday, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot met with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, to review bilateral relations and discuss regional developments. Barrot also reaffirmed France’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks.

Krieg assesses that France can offer Gulf states generally something that has become “increasingly valuable”: military capabilities not entirely dependent on the US.

“France can offer defence industrial cooperation, technology transfers, joint production, training and greater operational autonomy,” he said. “For countries such as the UAE and Qatar, this means progressively reducing their dependence on American weapons systems, spare parts, intelligence and political permissions.”

However, Krieg cautioned that the “central strategic dilemma” for France is likely to be whether increasing its involvement in the region could draw it into the ongoing conflict.

“Consider the protection of Saudi energy infrastructure against Houthi attacks,” he said. “French air defence systems intercepting missiles would directly undermine the Houthis’ military strategy. If French forces are subsequently targeted, Paris could face pressure to retaliate. What begins as a defensive deployment could gradually become an operational commitment with much wider implications.”

Krieg explained that the same is likely to apply to naval deployments around the Strait of Hormuz, adding that “escalation in one theatre can rapidly affect another”.

France’s ties with Iran have already been strained over tit-for-tat diplomatic expulsions and political rhetoric against each other.

In July and August, France strongly condemned Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

In July, two French Embassy staff members were detained in Tehran and then declared personae non gratae. Iran’s Foreign Ministry said the diplomats had “interfered in Iran’s internal affairs under the pretext of engaging with civil society”.

In August, French Foreign Minister Barrot expelled two Iranian diplomats in retaliation.

Speaking at the Global Security Forum in the Qatari capital, Doha, on Tuesday, US Envoy Tom Barrack said that Washington is moving away from its traditional security-for-oil relationship with the Middle East and no longer seeks to dominate the region.

“The US no longer wants to own,” said Barrack, who serves as US ambassador to Turkiye and special envoy for Syria. “The bargain is not to control, but to not leave. We’re not leaving.”

Barrack acknowledged that, following months of Iranian strikes on their infrastructure, regional partners are increasingly recognising the limits of US involvement.

Across the Middle East itself, defence partnerships have grown. In August, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed a trilateral security pact, also known as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. The pact has been activated amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

But there may now be an opening for other external actors – such as France – to find more of a role.

Krieg said Gulf states do not believe France will replace the US, whose military and intelligence infrastructure remains “unmatched”. Rather, they want a “diversified network of security partnerships”.

“France is particularly attractive because it possesses genuine expeditionary capabilities and has demonstrated a willingness to defend Gulf partners without joining Washington’s offensive campaign against Iran,” he said. “Its military presence has consequently acquired greater political significance.”

articles.title: Jane Doe says Cornell president appeared to question her allegations in letter to faculty senate
articles.summary: In the letter obtained by NBC News, Jane Doe said the university’s president seemed to brush off her report of a gang rape when he met with her sorority’s leader.
articles.body: Jane Doe, the woman who accused several Cornell University fraternity members of sexually assaulting her in 2024, sent a letter to the school’s faculty senate sharing a secondhand account of President Michael Kotlikoff’s response to her allegations ahead of a potential vote of no confidence in his administration. In a Wednesday letter obtained by NBC News, Doe described a meeting between Kotlikoff and the then-president of her sorority, Tri Delta, months after she reported the alleged assault to the university. Doe wrote that the sorority president subsequently told her that Kotlikoff had allegedly questioned why she waited to report the incident. “After the conversation she shared with me, with concern, that President Kotlikoff’s initial response was along the lines of, ‘Why did she wait so long to report it?’” Doe said in the letter. “She interpreted his question as an expression of doubt in the veracity of my story.” Cornell disputed that characterization Tuesday, saying in a statement that Kotlikoff’s question during a January 2025 meeting was focused on bystanders who had not reported the allegations, rather than Doe herself. The letter comes amid mounting scrutiny of Cornell’s handling of Doe’s allegations and growing debate among school faculty members over whether to hold a no-confidence vote in the university’s administration. Earlier this month, Cornell hired former acting U.S. Attorney General Sally Yates to lead an independent review, which will examine the school’s response to Doe’s allegations and broader policies governing sexual misconduct. In a civil lawsuit filed last month, Doe accused seven members of the now-dismantled Chi Phi fraternity of plying her with drugs and sexually assaulting her at a party in October 2024 and into the early hours of the next morning. Orazio Petito, who was named as the former president of the fraternity, was dropped from the lawsuit after his lawyer said he was “mistakenly” identified as the Chi Phi chapter president at the time of the alleged 2024 assault, according to court documents. Petito was not accused of assault in the lawsuit. Attorneys for several of the men have denied wrongdoing or disputed her account. Doe’s lawyer did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment. Cornell subsequently investigated the allegations through its Title IX disciplinary process, expelling two students and imposing suspensions or lesser sanctions on others. The university also launched a Presidential Task Force on Campus Sexual Assault in early 2025 and said in a statement Tuesday that it is implementing recommendations to improve its response to sexual misconduct. “The second-hand account of the question asked by President Kotlikoff in a January 2025 meeting in the letter is incorrect, based on a documented first-hand account,” the statement added. “The question ‘why did it take so long for the assault to be reported’ was directed at bystanders who did not use Cornell’s anonymous tip line, despite ongoing social media activity about the incident in October 2024. He was not questioning Jane Doe’s reporting.” In her letter, Doe wrote that the sorority president told her that at least one other faculty member who attended the meeting “appeared distressed” after hearing Kotlikoff’s question. Doe said that the faculty member thought “the President’s response was inappropriate.” “I felt unsupported and disbelieved by President Kotlikoff,” Doe wrote in the letter. “It diminished my confidence in the administration’s ability to approach my experience with the understanding, sensitivity, and fairness I had hoped for and expected from what had been my dream school.” Doe added that she is now sharing this account because she does not know how many people know about the meeting or the president’s response. “My intention is not to prescribe how the Senate should interpret this account, but rather to provide information that its members may wish to consider or investigate further,” she wrote. “I would not want to withhold something potentially pertinent, only for Senate members to later discover that information relevant to their deliberations had not been made available to them.” The letter has prompted questions from at least one faculty member about how it was handled by Cornell’s dean of faculty, Chris Schaffer. A professor on the faculty senate, who requested anonymity to speak freely about the situation, told NBC News that Schaffer told members Tuesday that he had received Doe’s letter last week, the same day the senate met to discuss whether to hold a vote of no confidence. “If he received it on the 14th, he should have said so,” the professor said. Cornell said Schaffer received the letter as “legal correspondence claiming to be from a law firm representing Jane Doe” and that he “subsequently turned it over to the General Counsel to verify and to share with the Independent Review.” “Shortly before the start of the Senate meeting on October 14, I received a communication from a lawyer representing Jane Doe, which relayed a second-hand account of President Kotlikoff asking about the timing of reports about the Jane Doe assault in 2024,” he wrote. “I later received a contemporaneous account of the meeting from a university official who was present that indicated President Kotlikoff asked bystanders ‘why did it take so long for the assault to be reported’ through Cornell’s anonymous tip line, given the level of social media discussion of the events. The question was not about Jane Doe or her decision to report.” Schaffer added that his office “does not have the investigatory capacity to properly follow up on private communications of this kind, nor is this the role of the office.” “In the interests of transparency, I am writing now to inform the Senate that I received this communication, that I passed it on to the Office of the General Counsel, and that they have sent it to the investigatory team led by Former Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates,” he added. “Any individual who has information they believe is relevant to the deliberation of the Cornell Senate may make such information public or communicate it directly.”

articles.title: Prince Harry says he wants to work out relationship with brother and father
articles.summary: Prince Harry has said he wants his disagreements with his brother Prince William and his father King Charles III to “work out.”
articles.body: LONDON — Prince Harry has said he wants his disagreements with his brother Prince William and his father King Charles III to “work out.” In an interview with GQ magazine about grief and family, recorded in New York in late September and published on Tuesday, Harry was asked if he grieves his “complicated” relationship with his father and brother. “Yes, of course,” he replied, adding that people often ask him about it because it’s a “massively relatable issue for so many people.” “Some people don’t want it to work out – I want it to work out,” he said. “Of course I do ... with everything else that’s going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile — that’s the key point.” Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children moved back to the U.K. in late August, six years after their decision to leave their roles as working royals and move to California widened a gulf in the royal family. The couple’s criticism in interviews included accusing an unspecified royal of racism and calling palace staff insensitive to Meghan’s mental health. But Harry, who is fifth in the line to the throne, said last year he would like to reconcile with his family and spend more time with his father, who is being treated for an undisclosed form of cancer. Asked if he thought he could repair the family rift, Harry told GQ: “Look, scars stick around forever,” but letting go of the past is “something that I would encourage everybody to do.” “For me, there’s enough drama in the world and enough drama in people’s lives than to continue with issues with family,” he added. A spokesperson later said his “some people” comment was “absolutely not intended as a swipe at his brother or any other member of his family.”

articles.title: 'We still feel unsafe in flood-prone Framlingham'
articles.summary: Residents want more to be done to protect their town from floods, three years on from Storm Babet.
articles.body:
Residents in a town devastated by a storm three years ago said they still felt unsafe and not truly protected from the risks of future flooding.

On 20 October 2023, Storm Babet resulted in many homes and businesses being flooded in Suffolk, along with countless schools closed and roads submerged.

Since then, local councils and agencies said they had carried out work to better safeguard parts of the county and support those affected.

But homeowners in Framlingham, which bore the brunt of the destructive weather along with Debenham, believed there was "a lot of progress yet to be made".

One of those residents is Chris Hobson, of Fairfield Road, who grabbed a suitcase and fled his house as "sentimental things got washed away".

Since then, he has spent tens of thousands of pounds to rebuild and safeguard his property, should something similar happen in future.

"We feel safer and better protected through our own financial output than we would have done before, but you can only do so much to protect your house," he said.

"You would hope that there was some sort of a plan. I know things are being looked at, but when you've been in that situation yourself, you just would like it to happen sooner rather than later."

Nick Cork, from Hour Community, has also taken measures to flood-proof the charity's headquarters.

He said he did still "worry" when storms were forecast and was "not sure a whole lot has changed" to protect Framlingham.

"Bits and pieces have been done, but if it happened again tomorrow, I think we'd be in exactly the same position," he told the BBC.

"There's a lot to be done to make us feel safe."

Explaining why Framlingham was flood-prone, Corke likened it to a saucer that can "catch quite a lot of water" and suggested "big cups around the edges" were needed.

That is something that local farmers in the area are hoping to establish in the form of natural hollows on their land, which can trap water and gradually empty it.

Bob Briscoe oversees one of 19 local farms looking to do their bit to better protect Framlingham, but funding is still required.

"The whole idea is when there's extreme rainfall, you're trying to hold back water above the towns and the villages upstream just enough," he said.

"We are all trying to help out, because we are the ones that are in a position to be able to help."

After the storm, Suffolk County Council, the lead local flood authority, commissioned a report to suggest actions to take to reduce future risks.

It has since increased resources in its flood investigations and grants team, which looks at the causes of flooding and collaborates with other councils and the Environment Agency.

In Debenham, the council recently completed natural flood management works upstream , to control the flow of surface water from the River Deben.

It said it continued to work with landowners and partners to "identify further opportunities for natural flood management across the county".

Meanwhile, East Suffolk Council said it had established a £500,000 Resilience and Emergency Response Fund, to ensure the council "can be more flexible and responsive to cover reasonable additional costs incurred by town and parish councils during an emergency event".

The authority said it had also appointed a "dedicated resilience officer", to improve community resilience to flooding.

An Environment Agency spokesperson said it was "working hard to safeguard the worst-affected areas, including boosting flood defences to 40 properties in Debenham, and improving warnings and flood management systems both here and in Framlingham".

The agency added it was updating its data to help manage future flood risk.

"Since the flooding of October 2023, comprehensive reviews of our flood warning system for Framlingham have been carried out," it said.

By doing this, the agency hoped "more properties may benefit from our warning service, and we have refined the thresholds we base our flood messaging on."

articles.title: Cinna calls out women over ‘misogynistic’ Sapphire Award debate, delays Streamer Awards vote
articles.summary: Twitch streamer Brittany “Cinna” has criticized women who are speaking against her chances of winning the Sapphire Award at The Streamer Awards 2026.
articles.body: Twitch streamer Brittany “Cinna” has criticized women who are speaking against her chances of winning the Sapphire Award at The Streamer Awards 2026. During her October 18 livestream, Cinna said she was “really disappointed” by the way some women were treating the award and using it to put other female streamers down. She also revealed that she planned to wait a few days before voting in this year’s awards. Cinna made it clear that her frustration was directed at viewers, not the streamers who had been nominated for the prize.Brittany “Cinna” Explains Why She Is Disappointed With Sapphire Award CriticismCinna spoke about the issue after seeing women on social media argue against her winning the Sapphire Award. She said some viewers were trying so hard to support other women that their behavior had become harmful to the same people they claimed to support.Explaining why she was delaying her vote, Cinna said:“I’m going to be honest - I want to do Streamer Awards voting this year. I think I’m going to. I think I will, but I’m going to give it a few days. But, like, bro, I’m like really disappointed in the amount of women, and I’m saying women because I’m seeing it a lot from the girls that are so... they are trying to girls-girls so hard that they’re misogynistic about the Sapphire Award.”She also explained that the way people were discussing the award had affected how she felt about it. However, she did not blame the award itself. Instead, she said some viewers were misunderstanding its purpose and using it to attack other women.Cinna explained:“It’s like... I don’t know, bro. I don’t know how to say that without saying it. But, like, it almost makes me dislike what the award has become, and I hate saying that. Right? Because I think the award is so good, and I love the award, and it’s not the award’s fault. But, like, I think some people misunderstand what the award is, and they’re so devout in, like, what they want their streamer to do, that they use the award to bring other women down. Not the streamers, to clarify the sczo... It’s the sczo viewers; it’s not the streamers.”Her clarification was important because she wanted people to understand that her criticism was about how certain viewers behaved online. She was not accusing the other nominees of encouraging attacks against her.Cinna Says Female Streamers Deserve to Be Celebrated for Their NominationsCinna continued by talking about how difficult it can be for streamers to reach the point where they receive an award nomination. She said the reaction from some online communities was disappointing, especially when the nominees were women who had worked hard to build their audiences.She also looked back at last year’s nominations and explained why she believed being nominated was something to celebrate.Cinna said:“It sucks to see that communities have gone that far, especially for women because I think the award is like... It’s cool that all these women got nominated. Even I felt the same way last year. I was like, it was stacked last year. Every single one of those girls should have been so happy that they got nominated. Do you know what that’s like? How hard it is to get to that point?”The Sapphire Award is one of the categories at The Streamer Awards, hosted by Blair “QTCinderella.” According to the nominees announced for 2026, Cinna is competing against Vanilla Mace, Yonna, Maya Higa, and Christinaandamber.The nominations were announced on October 16, while Cinna shared her reaction two days later. articles.title: 'Ant-Man' star Evangeline Lilly says she left Hollywood because she 'always hated being famous'
articles.summary: Evangeline Lilly says she secretly retired from Hollywood in 2020 after chronic health issues and a lifelong hatred of fame drove her away from acting.
articles.body: "Ant-Man" star Evangeline Lilly revealed in an interview with CBN News published Monday that she walked away from Hollywood six years ago despite a successful acting career, citing her longtime discomfort with fame, health problems and a desire to pursue a more meaningful life guided by her Christian faith. "I've always hated being famous," she said. "I never made any secrets about that. I've always said being famous is the cost of the wealth that you can get as an actor." The actress, best known for portraying Kate Austen in "Lost" and Hope van Dyne in Marvel's "Ant-Man" franchise, acknowledged experiencing moments of fear after walking away from the wealth, professional influence and recognition that accompanied her Hollywood success. "There has been definitely moments of fear of like, ‘How do you consciously and intentionally let go of so much seemingly power and influence and potentially money and also just affirmation of yourself,’" Lilly said. 'VAMPIRE DIARIES' STAR IAN SOMERHALDER SAYS LEAVING HOLLYWOOD FOR FARMING 'SHIFTED MY LIFE FOREVER' Christian Toto, a film critic and founder of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News Digital that Lilly's decision to leave her acting career is exceptionally rare, particularly for someone who achieved success in major Hollywood franchises. "It's extremely uncommon for stars to walk away from their acting careers," he said. "It happens, but it's the exception to the rule. Many work very hard to achieve a level of fame, so giving that up doesn't always make sense. For some, like Lilly, they learn that an actor's life has too many drawbacks, and they seek something more fulfilling." Despite those concerns, Lilly explained that her faith ultimately helped her embrace a future outside the entertainment industry's spotlight, saying she believed God had a greater purpose for her life beyond acting. "It's just been incredibly liberating and beautiful to step into a total trust and surrender that God has a plan for my life," Lilly said. "That that plan doesn't necessarily need to – it doesn't have to be about fame and money and wealth and power. It can be about more important things and that all of it works together." RICHARD GERE CONFRONTS HOLLYWOOD FAME, EGO AND GREED AS 'DARK CLOUDS' THAT THREATEN INNER PEACE Toto also said that celebrities face intense public scrutiny, arguing that social media has increased the personal pressures associated with Hollywood fame. "There's a cost to Hollywood fame," he said. "You live under the microscope. Strangers assume they know you and sometimes treat you that way in public. Your career is subjected to scrutiny in ways others can't imagine. It's always been so, but the rise of social media makes all of the above worse." The actress also revealed that leaving Hollywood significantly improved her physical and emotional well-being after years of struggling with chronic health issues she associated with the demands of her career. "My health has dramatically improved. I had massive chronic health issues by the time I retired," Lilly said. 'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WAS LOCKED IN PSYCH WARD AS HEALTH BATTLE SPIRALED Lily clarified that she had considered herself retired since 2020, four years before her departure attracted widespread media attention following a retrospective social media post in 2024. In June 2024, Lilly publicly announced she was stepping away from Hollywood by sharing a video recorded in 2006 in which she expressed her desire to retire from acting, raise a family and pursue humanitarian work. Toto suggested that Hollywood's treatment of older actresses could also influence decisions to leave the industry, particularly for women who have spent decades pursuing major acting roles.
